source.snippet: I keep track of one of our competitors by every day performing a site search on them on Google: site:competitor.com (last month). Typically Google indexes 5-10 new URLs for their site every day. I have also tried using Google Alerts... this alert only triggers a couple of times a week. Maybe I find on average 50 new URLs per week via manual search vs. almost nothing via Alerts. [1 score, 1 comment]

problem_statement: Marketing and competitive intelligence professionals who rely on Google Alerts for competitor content monitoring find it severely under-reports new indexed pages compared to manual site: searches, forcing expensive manual daily searches or expensive enterprise tools just to catch competitor content reliably.
target_segment: Marketing managers and competitive intelligence analysts at SMBs and agencies tracking competitor content and SEO activity daily
notes: Clear professional/business buyer context — person is doing daily competitive monitoring as a work task. Existing paid tools (Ahrefs Alerts, SEMrush brand monitoring) cost $100-400/mo and are overkill for this narrow need. A focused, affordable competitor content tracker that polls site: searches and sends reliable daily digests could fit a $20-50/mo niche. Recurring pain, paid buyer intent implied by professional workflow.
